main_body: Flat green ground tile patch (grass-like), repeating 16px motif of light-green clumps, dots and vertical strips on a mid-green base
top_band: none - terrain surface with no standing volume; a single column shows mid green with scattered light/dark green dots
evidence: Terrain tile kind: a flat ground fill with no standing volume, so the 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply. No isometric side faces and no object elevation. Terrain is acceptable as a flat repeating ground patch.

style.evidence: The candidate uses only about 3 greens (mid base, light clumps, dark dots). The 16px motif repeats identically 4x3 times with a visible grid-like pattern, unlike the Beodeul grass reference, which has varied tufts, several greens and soil grain. The base is a large flat mid-green fill between sparse motifs, and many tiles hold only 2-4 colours. It is thinner and more mechanical than the reference.
